name: Abhayagiri Dagoba
description: Major Buddhist monastery complex and one of the most important monasteries in ancient Sri Lanka.

name: Abu Simbel Temples
kingdom: New Kingdom of Egypt (The Imperial Age)
description: Twin colossal rock-cut temples carved into a sandstone mountain on the bank of the Nile in Nubia, guarded by four 20-meter seated colossi.
history: Erected by Ramesses II to commemorate his victory at the Battle of Kadesh and to honor Queen Nefertari. Relocated in an international UNESCO rescue operation in 1968 to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
construction: Carved directly into living sandstone bedrock; perfectly aligned so that twice a year the rising sun penetrates 65 meters inside to illuminate the statues in the sanctuary.
architecture: Monumental rock-cut facade featuring four giant enthroned figures of Ramesses II with the solar god Ra-Horakhty above the entrance.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; masterpiece of ancient Egyptian astronomical engineering.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved in Aswan Governorate, Egypt.

name: Angkor Wat (The City Temple)
description: The largest religious structure in world history, representing Mount Meru with five lotus towers surrounded by a massive 190-meter-wide moat.
history: Built as the state temple and royal funerary monument for Suryavarman II, gradually transitioning into a Buddhist pilgrimage site.
construction: Constructed from an estimated 5 million tonnes of sandstone quarried from Mount Kulen and floated down canals on balsa rafts.
architecture: Features concentric galleried enclosures, over 3,000 carved celestial Apsara dancers, and a continuous 800-meter outer wall of mythological bas-reliefs.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992 and national symbol of Cambodia.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved in Siem Reap, Cambodia.

name: Avukana Buddha Statue
description: Standing Buddha statue carved from a single granite rock, 40 feet tall.

name: Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı)
description: Subterranean cathedral-sized water reservoir supported by 336 marble columns, capable of storing 80,000 cubic meters of fresh water.
history: Filtered water from the Belgrade Forest for the Great Palace of Constantinople and the imperial court.
construction: Built with waterproof Roman brick-and-mortar masonry and repurposed classical columns, including two famous Medusa head bases.
architecture: Features 12 rows of 28 Corinthian and Ionic marble columns rising nine meters from the brick floor under vaulted brick cross-arches.
significance: Masterpiece of Byzantine civil and hydraulic engineering.
currentStatus: Open to the public as a museum in Istanbul, Turkey.

name: Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple of Thanjavur)
description: Colossal 66-meter Dravidian granite temple dedicated to Shiva, one of the Great Living Chola Temples.
history: Built by Rajaraja Chola to celebrate his imperial military conquests across South India and the Indian Ocean.
construction: Constructed entirely of interlocking granite blocks without mortar, capped by a single 80-tonne granite dome (Kumbam) lifted via a 6 km earthen ramp.
architecture: Features a 16-story pyramidal vimana tower, a colossal monolithic Nandi bull carved from a single stone, and vibrant Chola fresco paintings.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the crowning triumph of South Indian architecture.
currentStatus: Active place of worship and protected monument in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India.

name: Buduruwagala
description: Seven large rock-carved Buddha statues, the tallest being 51 feet.

name: Chichen Itza (El Castillo)
description: Astronomically aligned stepped pyramid of Kukulcan in Yucatán, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Major ceremonial city and political capital of the Terminal Classic Maya civilization, integrating Maya mathematics, geometry, and Toltec architectural artistry.
construction: Built of limestone masonry featuring 365 total steps (equaling days in the solar year), four 91-step staircases plus the top platform.
architecture: During the spring and autumn equinoxes, the setting sun casts a shadow across the pyramid that resembles a feathered serpent (Kukulcan) slithering down the balustrade.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.
currentStatus: Standing and actively conserved in Yucatán, Mexico.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted onto the official New 7 Wonders of the World roster on July 7, 2007, celebrated for its astronomical precision and Mesoamerican sacred geometry.

name: Colossus of Rhodes
description: Gigantic 33-meter bronze titan dedicated to the sun god Helios, an Ancient World Wonder.
history: Erected to commemorate the successful defense of Rhodes against a year-long siege by Demetrius Poliorcetes in 305 BCE. Financed by selling the abandoned siege engines and weaponry left behind by the besiegers.
construction: Crafted from melted siege bronze and iron over stone-weighted interior masonry towers, standing approximately 33 meters (108 feet) high at the harbor entrance.
architecture: Portrayed the sun god Helios with a radiant crown, holding a torch or spear overlooking Mandraki harbor.
significance: The tallest and most ambitious bronze statue in antiquity, inspiring future monuments including the Statue of Liberty.
currentStatus: Destroyed by the 226 BCE Rhodes earthquake after standing for only 54 years; the fallen bronze ruins lay undisturbed for 800 years until sold for scrap in 653 CE.
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Though standing for only 54 years before the 226 BCE earthquake broke its knees, an oracle warned the Rhodians against rebuilding it. Even in ruin, Pliny the Elder wrote that 'few men can clasp its thumb, and its fingers are larger than most statues.' In 653 CE, Arab caliphate forces sold the bronze to a merchant from Edessa.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
description: Largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka with over 150 Buddha statues.
history: King Valagamba took refuge in these caves for 14 years when he was exiled by South Indian invaders. Upon reclaiming his throne, he converted the caves into magnificent temples in gratitude.
construction: The complex consists of five main caves under a vast overhanging rock, rising 160 meters over the surrounding plains.
architecture: The cave ceilings are painted with intricate patterns and religious scenes covering 2,100 square meters. The complex houses 153 Buddha statues, 3 statues of Sri Lankan kings, and 4 statues of gods and goddesses.
significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site (1991), it is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in the country.
currentStatus: A major pilgrimage site and tourist attraction.

name: Ellora Caves & Kailasa Rock Temple
description: Cave 16 (Kailasa Temple) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, carved vertically downward from a solid basalt cliff.
history: Showcases 34 major monasteries and temples representing Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions carved side by side in religious harmony.
construction: Over 200,000 tonnes of basalt rock were chiseled away from top to bottom by hand over generations without scaffolds.
architecture: Full-scale Dravidian temple standing two stories high, adorned with life-sized elephant statues, columned mandapas, and mythological bas-reliefs.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983; an unparalleled feat of rock engineering.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Aurangabad District, Maharashtra, India.

name: Embekka Devalaya
description: Hindu temple famous for intricate wood carvings depicting dancers, musicians, and mythical creatures.

name: Erdene Zuu Monastery (Ancient Karakorum)
builtBy: Abtai Sain Khan (Built on ruins of Karakorum)
description: Oldest surviving Buddhist monastery in Mongolia, built within the perimeter walls of Karakorum, the 13th-century imperial capital of Genghis Khan.
history: Karakorum was founded by Genghis Khan in 1220 as the political hub from which the Mongol Empire commanded Eurasia.
construction: Enclosed by a massive 400x400 meter stone wall studded with 108 sacred Buddhist stupas.
architecture: Combines Chinese, Tibetan, and traditional Mongol nomadic architectural elements with preserved stone turtles.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape.
currentStatus: Active museum and monastery in Ovorkhangai Province, Mongolia.

name: Gadaladeniya Temple
description: Buddhist temple with South Indian architectural influences built on a rocky outcrop.

name: Gal Vihara
description: Group of four magnificent rock relief Buddha statues carved from a single granite rock wall.
history: Part of the Uttararama (Northern Monastery) commissioned by King Parakramabahu I. The chronicle Chulavamsa records the creation of these images.
construction: The four statues are carved into a single large granite rock face.
architecture: The complex includes a seated Buddha in deep meditation, a smaller seated Buddha inside a cave, a standing figure with crossed arms (often debated to be Ananda or the Buddha), and a massive reclining Buddha (14 meters long) depicting Parinirvana.
significance: Considered the masterpiece of Sinhalese rock carving. The fluid drapery and serene expressions demonstrate the peak of Polonnaruwa era artistry.
currentStatus: A protected archaeological site and an active place of worship.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
description: The largest sun-baked earth (adobe) building in the world, considered by many architects to be the crowning achievement of the Sudano-Sahelian style.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
description: The largest sun-dried mud brick (adobe) building in the world, the crowning masterwork of Sudano-Sahelian architecture on the Bani River.
history: Built when King Koi Kunboro converted to Islam, serving as a center of Islamic scholarship in West Africa alongside Timbuktu.
construction: Built of sun-baked mud bricks (ferey), sand, and organic plaster with palm wood beams (toron) projecting from the walls to serve as scaffolding for annual replastering.
architecture: Features three towering minarets topped with ostrich eggs (symbolizing fertility and purity) and a raised platform protecting from seasonal floods.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
currentStatus: Active place of worship in Djenné, Mali.

name: Great Pyramids of Giza & Great Sphinx
description: The oldest and only surviving monument of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
history: Constructed over 4,500 years ago during Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as a monumental tomb for Pharaoh Khufu. For over 3,800 years, it was the tallest man-made structure in the world.
construction: Composed of an estimated 2.3 million limestone and granite blocks weighing an average of 2.5 tons each, precisely aligned to true north with an error of less than one-tenth of a degree.
architecture: Features sophisticated internal corbelled chambers including the Grand Gallery, Queen's Chamber, and King's Chamber, surrounded by the mortuary complex and the colossal Great Sphinx.
significance: Designated an original Wonder of the Ancient World in the 2nd century BCE by Antipater of Sidon and Philo of Byzantium. Awarded permanent Honorary Wonder Status in the 2007 New 7 Wonders declaration.
currentStatus: Standing intact and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
wonderDesignationYear: c. 225 BCE (Antipater of Sidon Canon) & July 7, 2007 (Honorary Wonder)
wonderReplacedBy: Retained timeless honorary supremacy in the New 7 Wonders declaration
wonderHistoricalContext: Constructed c. 2560 BCE for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid was the first and oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. In 2007, when the New 7 Wonders campaign concluded in Lisbon, Giza was granted unique permanent Honorary Status, as it was the sole surviving monument from the original ancient canon.

name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
description: One of the oldest stone structures in India commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, featuring intricate torana gateways illustrating Buddhist jatakas.

name: Great Ziggurat of Ur
description: Massive stepped mud-brick pyramid temple dedicated to the moon god Nanna, built during the Neo-Sumerian revival.

name: Hagia Sophia (Church of Holy Wisdom)
description: The architectural crown of the Byzantine Empire, featuring a revolutionary 31-meter pendentive dome that seemed to 'hang suspended from the heavens'.
history: Served as the cathedral of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople for 900 years before becoming an Ottoman imperial mosque in 1453.
construction: Constructed in just five years using brick, mortar, and precious marbles from across the empire, adorned with gold glass mosaics.
architecture: First massive square basilica covered by a circular dome on four pendentives, creating an expansive interior light space.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; defined Eastern Christian and Ottoman architecture for 1,500 years.
currentStatus: Standing in Istanbul, Turkey.

name: Hampi (Group of Monuments at Vijayanagara)
description: Spectacular 4,100-hectare boulder-strewn capital city featuring over 1,600 surviving monuments, palaces, and hydraulic royal baths.
history: The capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, described by Portuguese and Persian visitors as one of the richest metropolises in the world.
construction: Engineered with local granite boulders, sophisticated aqueducts, and chariot shrines.
architecture: Features the Virupaksha Temple, the stone chariot of the Vittala Temple with musical pillars, and the Lotus Mahal.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.
currentStatus: Preserved archaeological complex in Bellary District, Karnataka, India.

name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
description: Legendary ascending multi-tiered botanical palace terraces, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
history: Reputedly built by King Nebuchadnezzar II for his Median wife Queen Amytis, who longed for the lush, forested mountains of her homeland. The gardens featured ascending series of tiered stone terraces with tropical flora and gravity-fed irrigation.
construction: Engineered with waterproofed vaulted stone foundations covered in bitumen, reeds, and baked brick, using innovative Archimedes screw-style water wheels lifting water from the Euphrates river.
architecture: Tiered ziggurat-like terraced structure rising over 23 meters into the air, creating the illusion of a floating mountain garden in the Mesopotamian desert.
significance: One of the canonical Seven Wonders of the Ancient World chronicled by Strabo, Diodorus Siculus, and Antipater of Sidon.
currentStatus: Destroyed after the 1st century CE due to earthquakes and warfare; archaeological excavations near Al-Hillah, Iraq continue to seek definitive structural foundations.
wonderStatus: Destroyed (after 1st century CE by earthquakes & erosion)
wonderReplacedYear: July 7, 2007 (Succeeded by New 7 Wonders Modern Registry)
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in the modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Celebrated in ancient Hellenistic literature for its unprecedented hydraulic irrigation and botanical grandeur. The gardens gradually fell into ruin after the fall of Babylon and were toppled by seismic tremors and Euphrates floods by the 1st century CE.

name: Himeji Castle (White Heron Castle)
description: Japan's most spectacular and best-preserved feudal samurai castle, renowned for its brilliant white plastered wooden walls.
history: Masterpiece of defensive castle architecture that survived the Meiji restoration, World War II bombings, and major earthquakes without damage.
construction: Built on a hill with high curving stone walls (Musha-gaeshi), 83 rooms, and intricate spiral maze defenses.
architecture: Six-story wooden keep with fireproof white plaster, projecting gables, and gun-slit arrow loops.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993; Japan's premier national treasure.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Himeji, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.

name: Ishtar Gate & Ruins of Babylon
description: The eighth inner gate of Babylon adorned with vibrant blue glazed bricks and bas-relief dragons (Mušḫuššu) and young bulls.

name: Isurumuniya Temple
description: Rock temple famous for the Isurumuniya Lovers sculpture and ancient carvings.

name: Jetavanaramaya
description: Once the tallest stupa in the ancient world, standing at 122 meters.
history: Built by King Mahasena following the destruction of the Mahavihara monastery, it was gifted to the Sagaliya sect. The construction marked a period of theological conflict between Theravada and Mahayana traditions in ancient Sri Lanka.
construction: Constructed using approximately 93 million baked bricks, it was the third tallest structure in the world upon completion, surpassed only by the Great Pyramids of Giza. Its original height was estimated at 122 meters (400 ft).
architecture: The stupa represents a massive engineering feat with a deep foundation resting on bedrock. It follows the traditional stupa architectural elements but on a colossal scale.
significance: It is the largest stupa in the world by volume and a testament to the advanced engineering capabilities of the Anuradhapura Kingdom.
currentStatus: Extensive conservation work by the Central Cultural Fund has stabilized the structure. It currently stands around 71 meters tall.

name: Karnak Temple Complex
kingdom: New Kingdom of Egypt (The Imperial Age)
builtBy: Pharaohs Senusret I to Ramesses II
description: The largest religious sanctuary of the ancient world, featuring the colossal Great Hypostyle Hall with 134 towering sandstone columns.
history: Dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu, it served as the political and religious epicenter of the Egyptian Empire.
construction: Spans over 100 hectares with sandstone blocks transported down the Nile from Gebel el-Silsila.
architecture: Features monumental pylons, towering obelisks of Hatshepsut, and the Hypostyle Hall with columns rising 21 meters high.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979; the pinnacle of Egyptian temple architecture.
currentStatus: Standing and open to the public in Luxor, Egypt.

name: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
description: An ancient Buddhist temple believed to have been hallowed during the third and final visit of the Lord Buddha to Sri Lanka. It was the capital of the regional King Kelanitissa. The temple is famous for its image house paintings and the annual Duruthu Perahera.

name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Iconic Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto covered in pure gold leaf, reflecting seamlessly across the Kyoko-chi mirror pond.

name: Kiri Vehera
description: Well-preserved white stupa built by the queen, still retaining its original lime plaster.

name: Lankarama
description: A stupa built by King Valagamba in an ancient place named Galhebakada. It is one of the eight sacred places (Atamasthana) in Anuradhapura. The stupa was originally surrounded by a vatadage (stupa house), of which only stone pillars remain.

name: Lankatilaka Temple
description: Ancient Buddhist temple built on a rock with impressive architecture.

name: Lighthouse of Alexandria (Pharos)
builtBy: Ptolemy I Soter and Ptolemy II Philadelphus
description: A pioneering 100-meter coastal navigational beacon, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
history: Constructed on the limestone island of Pharos at the port of Alexandria, the lighthouse was designed by Greek architect Sostratus of Cnidus. It guided merchant vessels across the Mediterranean for over a millennium using a polished bronze mirror by day and an open fire by night.
construction: Built in three cascading tiers: a square base, an octagonal middle section, and a cylindrical summit topped with a colossal statue of Poseidon or Zeus.
architecture: Constructed from massive blocks of white limestone held together with molten lead mortar, designed to withstand intense sea spray and gale-force Mediterranean storms.
significance: Became the universal archetype for all future lighthouses ('Pharos' remains the root word for lighthouse in French, Spanish, Italian, and Greek).
currentStatus: Severely damaged by earthquakes in 956, 1303, and 1323 CE; stones were salvaged in 1480 CE by Sultan Qaitbay to build the Citadel of Qaitbay.
wonderDesignationYear: c. 225 BCE (Philo of Byzantium & Antipater Lists)
wonderReplacedYear: 1480 CE (Citadel of Qaitbay built on ruins); July 7, 2007 (New 7 Wonders)
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced by modern world registry (New 7 Wonders of the World)
wonderHistoricalContext: Stood proudly as the world's tallest beacon for sixteen centuries until catastrophic earthquakes in 1303 and 1323 CE brought down its lantern. In 1480 CE, Mamluk Sultan Al-Ashraf Qaitbay built a defensive fortress directly over the remaining foundations using the fallen granite blocks.

name: Lovamahapaya (Brazen Palace)
description: Nine-storey monastic building said to have had a bronze roof with 1,600 granite columns.

name: Machu Picchu (Lost City of the Incas)
description: Spectacular 15th-century royal mountain citadel in the Peruvian Andes, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Constructed as a royal estate for Emperor Pachacuti atop a mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level. Abandoned around the time of the Spanish conquest and brought to global attention by Hiram Bingham in 1911.
construction: Constructed with dry-stone ashlar masonry where huge polished granite blocks fit together seamlessly without mortar, resilient to powerful Andean earthquakes.
architecture: Features over 200 agricultural terraces, residential compounds, ceremonial temples (Intihuatana astronomical stone), and cascading stone water fountains.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
currentStatus: Standing majestically preserved above the Urubamba Valley in Peru.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, representing the pinnacle of Incan stone masonry and harmonious mountain urban planning.

name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
description: Monumental tiered marble tomb that gave rise to the term 'mausoleum', an Ancient World Wonder.
history: Built in Halicarnassus (modern Bodrum, Turkey) for Mausolus, satrap of Caria under the Persian Empire. Conceived by his sister-wife Artemisia II, it was designed by Greek architects Satyros and Pythius, featuring sculptures by Leochares, Bryaxis, and Scopas.
construction: Stood 45 meters tall on a raised stone podium, enclosed by 36 Ionic columns and capped by a stepped pyramid with a colossal four-horse chariot statue at the pinnacle.
architecture: Fused Greek, Lycian, and Egyptian architectural traditions, embellished with three dynamic carved friezes depicting the Centauromachy and Amazonomachy.
significance: Its architectural triumph was so iconic that the word 'mausoleum' became the universal noun for all grand above-ground tombs.
currentStatus: Destroyed by a series of earthquakes between the 12th and 15th centuries CE; stones were reused by the Knights of St. John to construct Bodrum Castle in 1404 CE.
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Surviving unbroken for over 1,500 years until severe earthquakes fractured its columns. In 1404 CE, the Crusaders of St. John dismantled its remaining ruins to fortify the Castle of St. Peter in Bodrum.

name: Medirigiriya Vatadage
description: Ancient circular relic house with concentric stone columns and Buddha statues.

name: Mihintale
description: Sacred mountain where Buddhism was introduced to Sri Lanka by Mahinda.

name: Mirisawetiya Vihara
description: The first stupa built by King Dutugemunu after his victory over King Elara. Legend says the king went to bathe in the Tissa Wewa leaving his sceptre (kunta) with a Buddha relic planted in the ground. When he returned, it could not be moved, so he built the stupa over it.

name: Mogao Caves (Caves of the Thousand Buddhas)
description: Network of 492 cave sanctuaries carved into a cliff at the Silk Road junction of Dunhuang, housing 45,000 square meters of Buddhist murals.
history: Served as a spiritual nexus for merchants, pilgrims, and scholars traveling the Silk Road across the Gobi Desert.
construction: Carved into sandstone conglomerate cliffs, decorated with mineral pigments including lapis lazuli, malachite, and gold leaf.
architecture: Contains colossal seated Buddha statues up to 35 meters tall and the secret Library Cave (Cave 17) holding ancient manuscripts in multiple languages.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the world's richest repository of Silk Road art.
currentStatus: Protected in Dunhuang, Gansu Province, China.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel Island Abbey
builtBy: Bishop Aubert of Avranches and Capetian Kings
description: Gravity-defying Gothic Benedictine abbey perched atop a tidal granite island in Normandy, cut off from the mainland at high tide.
history: Major medieval Christian pilgrimage destination that withstood repeated English sieges during the Hundred Years' War.
construction: Constructed from granite transported across sand flats at low tide, engineered to follow the steep conical shape of the island rock.
architecture: Showcases 'La Merveille' (The Wonder)—a three-story masterpiece of Gothic architecture with a cloister suspended between sky and sea.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
currentStatus: Standing in Normandy, France.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: One of the most significant Hindu temples in Sri Lanka, dedicated to Lord Murugan. The original temple was founded in the 10th century but the current structure dates back to the 15th century, built by Sapumal Kumaraya (who later became King Bhuvanaikabahu VI of Kotte) during his administration of the Jaffna Kingdom.

name: Obelisk & Giant Stelae of Aksum
description: Colossal 24-meter single-block granite stele weighing 160 tonnes, carved with false doors and windows to represent multi-story palaces.
history: Served as royal funerary markers for the emperors of the ancient Kingdom of Aksum.
construction: Quarried from hard nepheline syenite granite 4 km away and rolled on logs before being hoisted into stone foundation sockets.
architecture: Single monolithic granite pillar carved with ten stories of false architectural timber frames.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980.
currentStatus: Standing in Aksum, Tigray Region, Ethiopia.

name: Palace of Versailles (Château de Versailles)
builtBy: King Louis XIV the Sun King
description: The ultimate symbol of French royal absolutism and European classical architecture, featuring the 73-meter Hall of Mirrors.
history: Transformed from a hunting lodge by Louis XIV into the seat of the French royal government from 1682 until the French Revolution in 1789.
construction: Employed 36,000 workers; features 2,300 rooms, 60,000 artworks, and 800 hectares of formal geometric gardens engineered with hydraulic fountains.
architecture: French Baroque masterpiece designed by Louis Le Vau, Jules Hardouin-Mansart, and landscape architect André Le Nôtre.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
currentStatus: Museum and national estate in Versailles, France.

name: Parakrama Samudra
description: Massive ancient irrigation reservoir demonstrating advanced hydraulic engineering.

name: Parthenon on the Acropolis
description: The quintessential Doric marble temple of Athena, an official New 7 Wonders Top Global Finalist.
history: Built during the Golden Age of Athens under Pericles as the centerpiece of the Acropolis complex, housing the giant chryselephantine statue of Athena Parthenos.
construction: Constructed from 20,000 tons of white Pentelic marble with subtle optical entasis curves so the lines appear perfectly straight to the human eye.
architecture: Peripteral octastyle Doric temple with Ionic frieze elements, pediment sculptures, and metopes depicting battles of gods, giants, and centaurs.
significance: The enduring global symbol of Western democracy, classical philosophy, and architectural harmony. Official Top 21 Finalist in the 2007 New 7 Wonders campaign.
currentStatus: Standing and conserved on the Acropolis rock in Athens.
wonderCategory: New7Wonders Top Global Finalist & Ancient Masterpiece
wonderHistoricalContext: Celebrated for 2,500 years as the highest peak of Greek classical architecture, finishing in the premier Top 21 Global Finalists in the official 2007 New 7 Wonders worldwide ballot.

name: Persepolis (Takht-e Jamshid)
builtBy: Darius I the Great and Xerxes I
description: Colossal terrace ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, ancient Wonder of the Near East.
history: Founded by Darius the Great in 518 BCE as the grand ceremonial capital where tributary nations from Egypt to India brought offerings during Nowruz (Persian New Year). Burned by Alexander the Great in 330 BCE.
construction: Built upon a massive 125,000 square meter stone terrace cut into Mount Rahmat, using precision iron-clamped limestone masonry without mortar.
architecture: Showcases the Gate of All Nations with colossal winged bull lamassu, the 72-column Apadana audience hall, and the Hall of a Hundred Columns.
significance: The crowning architectural achievement of the Achaemenid Empire; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
currentStatus: Preserved ruins and bas-reliefs near Shiraz, Iran.
wonderCategory: Ancient Wonder of Architecture (UNESCO World Heritage)
wonderHistoricalContext: Revered throughout the ancient world as the jewel of Persia. Its bas-reliefs depict peaceful processions of 23 subject nations, standing as the supreme wonder of Persian imperial architecture.

name: Petra (The Rose City)
builtBy: King Aretas IV and Nabataean Architects
description: Colossal rock-cut desert metropolis and trade capital, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Capital of the Nabataean Kingdom, situated in a desert canyon in southwestern Jordan. Controlled lucrative incense and spice trade routes between Arabia, Egypt, and the Levant.
construction: Carved directly into red and pink sandstone cliff faces, featuring advanced hydraulic water conduits, cisterns, and flash-flood bypass dams.
architecture: The iconic Al-Khazneh (The Treasury) and Ad-Deir (The Monastery) showcase Hellenistic-influenced classical facades carved out of natural bedrock.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
currentStatus: Standing and protected in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted onto the official New 7 Wonders list on July 7, 2007, celebrated as a triumph of desert hydrology and monumental rock-cut architecture.

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage
description: Circular relic house with finest stone carvings and moonstone entrances.
history: Built during the Polonnaruwa period to house the Tooth Relic. While some attribute it to Parakramabahu I, others suggest Nissanka Malla embellished it.
construction: A circular structure with two concentric stone terraces.
architecture: Famous for its moonstones (sandakada pahana) and guardstones (muragala) which are considered the finest examples of Polonnaruwa art. Four seated Buddha statues face the four cardinal directions.
significance: It is the best-preserved example of a 'Vatadage' (circular relic house) in Sri Lanka.
currentStatus: A well-preserved archaeological ruin in the Dalada Maluwa (Quadrangle) of Polonnaruwa.

name: Pompeii Archaeological Park
description: Vibrant ancient Roman city frozen in time under meters of volcanic ash during the catastrophic eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE.
history: Discovered in the 18th century, Pompeii offers an extraordinary snapshot of daily Roman life, featuring streets, taverns, villas, frescoes, and mosaics.
construction: Constructed with volcanic tuff masonry, terracotta piping, and Roman concrete with lead water mains.
architecture: Features the Forum, amphitheatre, thermal baths, and lavish domus villas like the House of the Faun.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997; the world's premier window into Roman urban civilization.
currentStatus: Excavated and open to the public in Campania, Italy.

name: Pyramids of Teotihuacan
description: Ancient holy city featuring the monumental Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, and the Avenue of the Dead.

name: Pyramids of Teotihuacan (City of the Gods)
description: Monumental ancient Mesoamerican metropolis centered around the Avenue of the Dead, the Pyramid of the Sun, and the Pyramid of the Moon.
history: One of the largest cities in the ancient world with over 125,000 residents; revered centuries later by the Aztecs as the sacred birthplace of the Fifth Sun.
construction: Built with millions of tons of volcanic stone, lime plaster, and talud-tablero architectural layering.
architecture: The Pyramid of the Sun stands 65 meters high with a base footprint comparable to the Great Pyramid of Giza.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
currentStatus: Preserved archaeological park in State of Mexico, Mexico.

name: Rankot Vehera
description: Fourth largest stupa in Sri Lanka and largest in Polonnaruwa.

name: Ritigala Monastery
description: Ancient forest monastery complex with unique architectural features.

name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela (Bete Giyorgis)
description: Eleven monolithic medieval Christian churches chiseled out of solid volcanic basalt bedrock, connected by subterranean stone trenches and catacombs.
history: Built by King Lalibela to create a 'New Jerusalem' in Ethiopia after Muslim conquests halted pilgrimage routes to the Holy Land.
construction: Chiseled vertically down into living reddish volcanic tuff; Bete Giyorgis (Church of St. George) was carved as a perfect Greek cross 12 meters deep without adding any external stones or mortar.
architecture: Features intricate Greek and Maltese cross reliefs, arched windows, and subterranean drainage conduits.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978; an eighth wonder of medieval religious engineering.
currentStatus: Active pilgrimage site in Amhara Region, Ethiopia.

name: Royal Palace of Polonnaruwa
description: Seven-storey royal palace complex with impressive architectural remains.

name: Ruins of Pompeii
description: Remarkably preserved Roman city buried under volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE, providing vivid insight into daily imperial life.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
description: One of the world's tallest ancient monuments and a masterpiece of Sinhalese engineering.
history: Commissioned by the hero-king Dutugemunu to enshrine sacred relics, Ruwanwelisaya (The Great Stupa) was his magnum opus. The Mahavamsa records that the king fell ill and passed away just before its completion; his brother Saddha Tissa covered the unfinished dome with white cloth to show the dying king what it would look like.
construction: Originally standing at 103 meters (338 ft) with a circumference of 290 meters, it was one of the tallest structures in the ancient world. The foundation was stabilized using crushed stone and elephants equipped with leather boots to stomp the ground flat.
architecture: The stupa follows the 'Bubulakara' (bubble-shaped) design. It features a 'vahalkada' (frontispiece) at each of the four cardinal points, adorned with elephant carvings. The 'Hatharas Kotuwa' (square enclosure) and 'Devatha Kotuwa' (deity enclosure) sit atop the dome.
significance: It is revered as the 'Mahathupa' (Great Stupa) and is one of the Solosmasthana (16 sacred places) and Atamasthana (8 sacred places) in Anuradhapura. It is believed to house the largest collection of Buddha's relics in the world.
currentStatus: A major pilgrimage site for Buddhists globally, the stupa was renovated in the early 20th century and stands today at 103 meters.

name: Sacsayhuamán Megalithic Citadel
description: Colossal zig-zag megalithic stone citadel overlooking Cusco, featuring individual polished limestone blocks weighing over 120 tonnes.
history: Served as the military fortress guarding the royal capital of Cusco and the ceremonial arena for the Inti Raymi (Festival of the Sun).
construction: Constructed with precision dry-stone ashlar masonry where massive polygonal stones fit together so tightly that a sheet of paper cannot pass between them.
architecture: Three tiers of zig-zagging stone terrace ramparts designed in the shape of lightning and the teeth of the Cusco puma.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the City of Cusco.
currentStatus: Standing in Cusco Region, Peru.

name: Sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi
description: The sacred center ('omphalos' or navel) of the ancient Greek world, home to the revered Pythian Oracle of Apollo.
history: Leaders from every Greek city-state and foreign kings consulted the Pythia priestess before waging war or establishing colonies.
construction: Perched on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, featuring Doric stone temples, treasury houses, an open-air theatre, and athletic stadium.
architecture: Features the Temple of Apollo, Athenian Treasury, the circular Tholos of Delphi at the sanctuary of Athena Pronaia.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the spiritual heartbeat of pan-Hellenic unity.
currentStatus: Preserved archaeological park in Phocis, Greece.

name: Sankore University & Djinguereber Mosque
description: Historic mud-and-timber center of Islamic learning in Timbuktu that educated over 25,000 scholars with a library of hundreds of thousands of manuscripts.
history: Commissioned by Mansa Musa upon his return from Mecca in 1324, transforming Timbuktu into the intellectual capital of the Sahara.
construction: Constructed with earth, limestone mortar, and indigenous acacia wood frameworks.
architecture: Features pyramidal minarets, shaded cloistered courtyards, and massive earthen prayer halls.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
currentStatus: Protected in Timbuktu, Mali.

name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress (Lion Rock)
description: Monumental 200-meter sheer monolith citadel, globally acclaimed as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.
history: Constructed by King Kashyapa I as an impregnable royal citadel and pleasure palace after taking the throne. Features a lion-shaped gateway, mirror-polished gallery wall, and celestial damsel frescoes.
construction: Built atop a 200-meter vertical granite inselberg with complex gravity-fed hydraulic water gardens, tiered subterranean pipes, and moated defenses.
architecture: Features the oldest surviving landscaped water gardens in Asia, dynamic wind-cooled rock chambers, and the iconic Mirror Wall with 8th-century visitor graffiti.
significance: Acclaimed worldwide as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved by the Central Cultural Fund of Sri Lanka.
wonderCategory: Eighth Wonder of the World (UNESCO & Global Acclaim)
wonderHistoricalContext: Celebrated by archaeologists and historians across the globe as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' due to its visionary 5th-century urban planning, hydraulic pressure fountains that still function during rains, and sky palace.

name: Sri Maha Bodhi
description: Sacred fig tree grown from a cutting of the original Bodhi tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment.

name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
description: Colossal 12.4-meter chryselephantine statue of the king of Greek gods, an Ancient World Wonder.
history: Commissioned by the Eleans for the sanctuary at Olympia, the statue was sculpted by Phidias. Zeus sat upon an elaborate cedarwood throne ornamented with ebony, ivory, gold, and precious gemstones, holding Nike (goddess of victory) in his right hand.
construction: Framed with wood and paneled with sculpted ivory plates for flesh and beaten sheets of solid gold for drapery (chryselephantine technique).
architecture: The statue occupied the entire width of the cella aisle in the Temple of Zeus, appearing so grand that ancient writers remarked if Zeus stood up, he would unroof the temple.
significance: The crowning achievement of ancient Greek classical sculpture and an essential pilgrimage destination during the Ancient Olympic Games.
currentStatus: Destroyed in the 5th century CE by fire (either at Olympia in 426 CE or during the Palace of Lausus fire in Constantinople in 475 CE).
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Admired across the Greco-Roman world for eight centuries. After the abolition of the Olympic Games by Christian Emperor Theodosius I, the statue was relocated to Constantinople, where it perished in a palace conflagration in 475 CE.

name: Stonehenge Megalithic Monument
description: Iconic prehistoric megalithic stone circle aligned to the solstices, historic Wonder of the Medieval World.
history: Constructed in several stages over a thousand years on Salisbury Plain. Aligned with the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice.
construction: Constructed using sarsen stones weighing up to 25 tons and bluestones transported over 225 km from the Preseli Hills in Wales using mortise-and-tenon joints.
architecture: Sophisticated outer ring of vertical sarsen megaliths connected by horizontal lintel stones, surrounding an inner horseshoe of giant trilithons.
significance: Listed in medieval chronicles among the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages and reached the Top 21 Finalists in the 2007 New 7 Wonders campaign.
currentStatus: Standing and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.
wonderCategory: Seven Wonders of the Medieval World & New7Wonders Finalist
wonderHistoricalContext: Chronicled in medieval European wonder lists and confirmed as an official Top 21 Global Finalist in the 2007 New 7 Wonders campaign.

name: Sultan Ahmed Mosque (The Blue Mosque)
builtBy: Sultan Ahmed I (Architect: Sedefkar Mehmed Agha)
description: Iconic Ottoman imperial mosque featuring six slender minarets and an interior lined with over 20,000 handmade blue Iznik ceramic tiles.
history: Constructed to reassert Ottoman imperial prestige following wars with Persia and the Habsburgs.
construction: Built directly opposite Hagia Sophia, integrating classical Ottoman dome geometry with Byzantine pendentive design.
architecture: Features a central dome 43 meters high flanked by four semi-domes and 260 stained-glass windows.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; masterpiece of Islamic architectural symmetry.
currentStatus: Active place of worship and historic monument in Istanbul, Turkey.

name: Taj Mahal
description: Peerless white Makrana marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan to house the remains of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built over 22 years by an army of 20,000 artisans under the direction of court architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
construction: Crafted from translucent white Makrana marble inlaid with 28 varieties of precious and semi-precious stones (pietra dura technique) and flanked by red sandstone mosques.
architecture: Flawless bilateral symmetry, a central double dome rising 73 meters, four detached minarets angled outward, and a formal Charbagh Persian paradise garden.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and described by Rabindranath Tagore as 'a teardrop on the cheek of eternity.'
currentStatus: Standing pristine and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
wonderHistoricalContext: Declared an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, recognized worldwide as the pinnacle of Indo-Islamic architectural symmetry and devotion.

name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
builtBy: Croesus of Lydia / Chersiphron / Alexander the Great
description: Colossal marble sanctuary with 127 ionic columns, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
history: Dedicated to Artemis, goddess of fertility and the hunt, the temple was funded by the wealthy King Croesus of Lydia. Arsoned in 356 BCE by Herostratus on the night Alexander the Great was born, it was rebuilt on an even grander scale with Alexander's backing.
construction: Built entirely of white marble spanning 137 meters in length and 69 meters in width, featuring 127 carved columns standing 18 meters high.
architecture: Magnificent Ionic dipteral temple surrounded by a double row of columns adorned with bas-reliefs by renowned sculptors Scopas and Polyclitus.
significance: The largest temple in the Hellenistic world, serving as a religious sanctuary, financial bank, and cultural trade nexus.
currentStatus: Destroyed in 401 CE by a mob led by St. John Chrysostom; only a single reconstructed composite column remains at the site near Selçuk, Turkey.
wonderReplacedBy: Replaced in modern global canon by the New 7 Wonders campaign
wonderHistoricalContext: Antipater of Sidon wrote: 'When I saw the sacred house of Artemis that towers to the clouds, the other Wonders were placed in the shade.' It was pillaged by Goths in 268 CE and finally dismantled in 401 CE.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
description: Temple housing the relic of the tooth of Buddha, UNESCO World Heritage Site.
history: The Sacred Tooth Relic (Dalada) was brought to Sri Lanka in the 4th century CE. It became the palladium of kingship—whoever possessed it had the divine right to rule. The current two-story shrine was built by King Sri Veera Parakrama Narendrasinghe (1707-1739), with later additions by the last king, Sri Vikrama Rajasinha (the Octagon).
construction: The temple complex is located within the royal palace grounds. It is built on a granite base with walls of limestone and timber upper floors.
architecture: The architecture features typical Kandyan elements: a high-pitched roof, white walls with cloud drift walls (Walakulu Bemma), and the famous Octagon (Paththirippuwa). The interior is richly decorated with ivory, lacquer work, and intricate wood carvings.
significance: It is the most sacred Buddhist site in Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The annual Esala Perahera procession centers around the relic.
currentStatus: It remains a center of daily worship and a major tourist attraction. The relic is kept in seven nesting gold caskets.

name: Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang
description: Subterranean army of 8,000 unique life-sized soldiers, acclaimed as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.
history: Constructed to guard the first Emperor of unified China, Qin Shi Huang, in the afterlife. Discovered by local farmers in Lintong District, Xi'an in 1974.
construction: Over 700,000 workers molded and fired individual terracotta figures, each with distinct facial features, hairstyles, armor, and bronze weaponry.
architecture: Massive four-pit subterranean necropolis covering over 56 square kilometers, originally painted in vibrant cinnabar, malachite, and azurite pigments.
significance: Acclaimed worldwide as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World' following French Prime Minister Jacques Chirac's declaration in 1978; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
currentStatus: Excavated and displayed in the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum.
wonderCategory: Eighth Wonder of the World (International Acclaim)
wonderHistoricalContext: In 1978, during an official state visit, French statesman Jacques Chirac declared: 'There were Seven Wonders in the world, and the discovery of the Terracotta Army is the Eighth.' It remains universally recognized under this title.

name: The Bayon (Temple of Smiling Faces)
description: Atmospheric Mahayana Buddhist state temple at the center of Angkor Thom, famous for 216 gigantic serene stone faces of Avalokiteshvara.
history: Built by King Jayavarman VII as the spiritual heart of his walled capital city following the expulsion of Cham invaders.
construction: Constructed of sandstone blocks with three cascading architectural levels crowned by a central circular sanctuary.
architecture: Features 54 gothic towers with four smiling faces carved on each side, surrounded by bas-reliefs depicting daily 12th-century Khmer market life and naval battles.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site; one of the most enigmatic temple structures on Earth.
currentStatus: Standing in Angkor Thom, Siem Reap, Cambodia.

name: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre)
description: Colossal four-tiered elliptical amphitheatre in Rome, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Commissioned by Emperor Vespasian in 70 CE and inaugurated by Titus in 80 CE with 100 days of games. Hosted gladiatorial combats, wild animal hunts, and mock naval battles for up to 65,000 spectators.
construction: Built from travertine limestone, tuff volcanic stone, brick-faced concrete, and over 100,000 cubic meters of marble held by iron clamps.
architecture: Pioneered monumental barrel vaulting, hypogeum underground staging elevators, and layered Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian exterior arcades.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World in 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
currentStatus: Standing iconic landmark in the heart of Rome.
wonderHistoricalContext: Selected on July 7, 2007 as one of the New 7 Wonders of the World, standing as the eternal symbol of Roman architectural and civil engineering prowess.

name: The Forbidden City (Imperial Palace)
description: The world's largest palatial complex, spanning 720,000 square meters with 980 surviving buildings and 8,886 bays of rooms.
history: Served as the home of 24 Chinese emperors across the Ming and Qing Dynasties from 1420 to 1924 CE.
construction: Built by over one million workers using precision interlocking timber bracket joinery (Dougong) without a single iron nail.
architecture: Strict North-South axial Feng Shui alignment, yellow glazed imperial roof tiles, white marble terraces, and deep crimson walls.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the supreme monument of traditional Chinese architecture.
currentStatus: Standing pristine as the Palace Museum in the heart of Beijing.

name: The Great Wall of China
description: Massive 21,196 km military defensive fortification network, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Built and continuously expanded across successive Chinese dynasties to protect against nomadic raids and secure Silk Road trade. The most prominent surviving stone brick sections were built during the Ming Dynasty.
construction: Constructed from tamped earth, granite, limestone, and kiln-fired bricks held together by sticky rice mortar.
architecture: Features defensive watchtowers, beacon signaling towers, garrison fortresses, and tactical crenellations across mountainous terrain.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved across multiple provinces in northern China.
wonderHistoricalContext: Chosen by over 100 million global voters in Lisbon on July 7, 2007 (07/07/07) as a premier New 7 Wonder of the World, representing humanity's greatest defensive engineering achievement.

name: The Pantheon
description: Former Roman temple featuring the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, crowned by an open central oculus.
history: Commissioned by Marcus Agrippa during the reign of Augustus and completely rebuilt by Emperor Hadrian c. 126 CE.
construction: Engineered with volcanic pozzolana concrete that gradually lightens in density toward the top using pumice aggregates.
architecture: Octastyle Corinthian portico opening into a rotunda of exact proportion: the interior height and diameter are equal at 43.3 meters.
significance: The best-preserved Roman monument in existence and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Piazza della Rotonda, Rome.

name: The Tower of London (Her Majesty's Fortress)
description: Historic stone castle and royal fortress on the north bank of the River Thames, home to the Crown Jewels and 1,000 years of royal history.
history: Built by William the Conqueror to protect and dominate London; served as a royal residence, prison, armory, mint, and menagerie.
construction: Centered around the massive stone White Tower built with Caen limestone imported from Normandy.
architecture: Concentric fortress with inner and outer defensive curtain walls, water-gate (Traitors' Gate), and 21 towers.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Central London, England.

name: Thuparamaya
description: First Buddhist stupa built in Sri Lanka, enshrining the right collarbone of Buddha.

name: Tikal Temple I (Temple of the Great Jaguar)
description: Towering 47-meter limestone stepped pyramid rising above the Petén jungle canopy, built as the mortuary temple for King Jasaw Chan K'awiil I.
history: Tikal was the dominant superpower of the Classic Maya lowlands, controlling extensive trade routes and defeating its rival Calakmul.
construction: Constructed from locally quarried limestone blocks with nine stepped tiers representing the nine levels of the Maya underworld (Xibalba).
architecture: Features a steep 70-degree central stairway crowned by a three-room shrine and a carved wooden roof comb.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979; quintessential symbol of Maya civilization.
currentStatus: Protected in Tikal National Park, Petén, Guatemala.

name: Todai-ji Temple (Eastern Great Temple)
description: Monumental Buddhist temple housing the Daibutsu (15-meter bronze Great Buddha), one of the world's largest wooden buildings.
history: Constructed by Emperor Shomu to bring national unity, peace, and spiritual protection to Japan after epidemics and rebellions.
construction: Built from massive ancient cedar pillars and bronze casting using an estimated 500 tonnes of copper, tin, and gold leaf.
architecture: Massive hip-and-gable roof structure with double eaves and dramatic golden Shibi roof ridge ornaments.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara.
currentStatus: Active temple and national treasure in Nara, Japan.

name: Topkapi Palace (Saray-ı Hümayun)
description: Grand imperial administrative and residential palace of the Ottoman Sultans overlooking the Bosphorus and Golden Horn.
history: Served as the administrative center and royal residence of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years from 1465 to 1856 CE.
construction: Spans four cascading courtyards with pavilions, the Imperial Harem, treasury, and the Chamber of Holy Relics.
architecture: Features classic Ottoman Iznik tilework, mother-of-pearl inlay, and the iconic Tower of Justice.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Historic Areas of Istanbul.
currentStatus: Museum complex in Istanbul, Turkey.

name: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
description: Rock fortress with ornate staircase that once housed the Sacred Tooth Relic.
